# theirs: batched_arima.cu d_y_p[0] = 0.0 (:207)
why / where it would go: It is the first statement of the per-series lambda and writes element 0 of the WHOLE output, from every one of batch_size threads. Thread 0 writes the real d_y_p[0] later inside its own loop, but threads bid > 0 are unordered against it and any of them can land its 0.0 afterwards, so d_y_p[0] can come back 0.0 instead of the prediction or the NaN sentinel for any batch of more than one series. A genuine data race with an observable result. assume-our-code-is-broken says fix their bug rather than mirror it; the fix is to not write the cell

why / where it would go: Theirs computes it at batched_kalman.cu:1088-1089 and matrix.cuh:1876 and NEVER CHECKS it, so a singular I - T (x) T produces an unusable P0 silently. Ours returns it from lu_inverse and the host raises by name with the failing column

# theirs: cuBLAS getrf / getri / gemm themselves
why / where it would go: Closed calls with no MAX equivalent for a batched LU. Their association order and their pivot tie rule are not readable from source, so the spelling here is chosen and written down rather than inherited: pivot = FIRST index of the strictly largest magnitude in the column (a strict `>` scan, so no signed zero can displace the other), row swap, L column = a / pivot, trailing update fma(-l, u, a), then the inverse column by column by permuted forward and backward substitution, serial ascending. That the tie rule is OURS and not theirs is exactly why sabotage (e) in SABOTAGES.md perturbs it

why / where it would go: The kernel writes all `parameter` cells for every model < batchSize, and nElements is batchSize * parameter, so every copied cell is overwritten before it is read. Recorded rather than dropped silently
